title: Your $5 Coffee Could Cost You $300,000 ☕ #shorts
description:
$5 a day is $1,825 a year, about $54,750 in cash over 30 years. Invested at the S&P 500's long-run average of about 10% a year, it could grow to around $300,000 (about $157K-$172K in today's money at 6.5-7% after inflation). Past returns are not guaranteed. Education, not financial advice.
Source: David Bach, "The Latte Factor" / "The Automatic Millionaire"; S&P 500 average return: Fidelity Learning Center and NerdWallet (2026); future value calculated with the standard annuity formula.
script: Your five dollar coffee could be costing you three hundred thousand dollars.
Author David Bach called it the latte factor.
Five dollars a day is about eighteen hundred dollars a year.
Over thirty years, that's almost fifty-five thousand dollars in plain cash.
But invest it instead, at the stock market's long-run average of about ten percent a year.
Compounding turns it into around three hundred thousand.
Even after inflation, that's still well over one hundred fifty thousand in today's money.
The coffee isn't the real problem. Small leaks, every single day, quietly cost you a fortune.
